# terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns/commits)


Terraform module that manages the Amazon Route53 DNS records fronting an application
environment — typically an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment, but any CNAME or alias
target works. It resolves the hosted zone by name, then creates exactly one record of
the variant selected by the input combination: a plain CNAME, a weighted CNAME, an
alias `A` record, or a weighted alias `A` record — with optional Route53 health check
association.

## Introduction

Publishing an application environment behind a friendly hostname usually means the same
handful of Route53 decisions over and over: is this a CNAME or an alias, is traffic
weighted across environments, and is the target health checked. This module encapsulates
those decisions behind a small, flat input surface so a deployment only declares intent.

### Record selection

The module never creates more than one record. Which one it creates is decided by two
inputs — `domain_alias` and `domain_name_weight`:

| `domain_alias` | `domain_name_weight` | Resource created            | Record type |
|----------------|----------------------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| `false`        | `< 0`                | `app_record_plain`          | `CNAME`     |
| `false`        | `>= 0`               | `app_record_weighted`       | `CNAME`     |
| `true`         | `< 0`                | `app_record_alias`          | `A` (alias) |
| `true`         | `>= 0`               | `app_record_alias_weighted` | `A` (alias) |

In every case the record name is `<domain_name_alias_prefix>.<domain_name>` and the
target is `alias_cname`.

### Weighted routing

Setting `domain_name_weight` to a value greater than or equal to `0` switches the module
into weighted routing. The record set identifier is derived as
`<release_name>-<namespace>`, which keeps sibling environments — for example `blue` and
`green`, or two regional deployments — distinct inside the same record set. A negative
weight (the default, `-1`) means simple routing and no set identifier.

### Alias records

When `domain_alias` is `true` the module emits a Route53 alias `A` record instead of a
`CNAME`. Alias records let the apex of a zone point at an AWS resource and are not
billed per query. This mode requires `alias_zone_id` — the hosted zone ID of the *target*
resource, not of your own zone. A `precondition` fails the plan with a clear message if
it is left empty.

### Health checking

`domain_check_target` controls health check behaviour and applies to all four variants:

- With `health_check_id` set, that health check is associated with the record.
- With `health_check_id` empty and the record being an alias, `evaluate_target_health`
  is enabled so Route53 follows the health of the alias target itself.
- With `domain_check_target = false`, no health check is associated at all.

### Public and private zones

The hosted zone is resolved by name through a `aws_route53_zone` data source, so the zone
must already exist. Set `private_domain = true` to resolve a private hosted zone instead
of a public one — useful when the same domain name is served by both a public and a
private zone in the same account.

## Usage


**IMPORTANT:** The `master` branch is used in `source` just as an example. In your code, do not pin to `master` because there may be breaking changes between releases.
Instead pin to the release tag (e.g. `?ref=vX.Y.Z`) of one of our [latest releases](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns/releases).


This module is consumed through [Terragrunt](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/) using the
built-in `scaffold` command, which reads `.boilerplate/boilerplate.yml` from this
repository and generates `terragrunt.hcl`, `inputs.yaml` and `local-tags.json` into your
deployment directory.

### 1. Scaffold the deployment

```sh
# Create and enter the target deployment directory
mkdir -p <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/beanstalk-dns
cd <environment>/<region>/<spoke>/beanstalk-dns

# Scaffold the module (do NOT use --working-dir)
terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns

# Edit inputs.yaml with deployment-specific values
vi inputs.yaml

# Apply
terragrunt apply
```

### 2. Fill in `inputs.yaml`

Scaffold writes the annotated file below. Every key carries its `(Required)` /
`(Optional)` marker and default, so no Terraform source needs to be read to configure a
deployment.

```yaml
# --- Provider ---------------------------------------------------------------
region: "us-east-1"           # (Optional) AWS region the provider operates in. Default is "us-east-1".
sts_assume_role: ""           # (Required) ARN of the IAM role assumed by the AWS provider.

# --- Record identity --------------------------------------------------------
release_name: "myapp"         # (Required) Release name of the deployed application. Combined with namespace to build the weighted record set identifier.
namespace: "dev"              # (Required) Namespace that determines the environment naming.

# --- Hosted zone ------------------------------------------------------------
domain_name: "example.com"    # (Optional) Route53 hosted zone name the record is created in. Must already exist. Default is "example.com".
private_domain: false         # (Optional) Look the hosted zone up as a private zone. Values: true | false. Default is false.

# --- Record definition ------------------------------------------------------
domain_name_alias_prefix: ""  # (Optional) Host prefix prepended to domain_name, as in "<prefix>.<domain_name>". Default is "" (empty).
alias_cname: ""               # (Optional) Target the record points to: CNAME value, or alias target DNS name. Default is "" (empty).
default_domain_ttl: 300       # (Optional) TTL in seconds for CNAME records. Ignored for alias records. Default is 300.

# --- Routing policy ---------------------------------------------------------
domain_name_weight: -1        # (Optional) Weight for weighted routing. >= 0 creates a weighted record; negative creates a simple record. Default is -1.

# --- Alias records ----------------------------------------------------------
domain_alias: false           # (Optional) Create an alias A record instead of a CNAME. Requires alias_zone_id. Default is false.
alias_zone_id: ""             # (Optional) Route53 hosted zone ID of the alias target. Required when domain_alias is true. Default is "" (empty).

# --- Health checking --------------------------------------------------------
domain_check_target: true     # (Optional) Associate a health check with the record. Default is true.
health_check_id: ""           # (Optional) ID of an existing Route53 health check. Applied only when domain_check_target is true. Default is "" (empty).
```

### 3. Generated `terragrunt.hcl`

Scaffold produces the file below — it is shown for reference and should not be
hand-authored. `inputs.yaml` is loaded as `local.local_vars` and mapped into the module
inputs, while `is_hub`, `org`, `spoke_def` and `extra_tags` are resolved from the
surrounding Terragrunt hierarchy.

```hcl
locals {
  local_vars  = yamldecode(file("./inputs.yaml"))
  spoke_vars  = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("spoke-inputs.yaml")))
  region_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("region-inputs.yaml")))
  env_vars    = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-inputs.yaml")))
  global_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-inputs.yaml")))

  local_tags  = jsondecode(file("./local-tags.json"))
  spoke_tags  = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("spoke-tags.json")))
  region_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("region-tags.json")))
  env_tags    = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-tags.json")))
  global_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-tags.json")))

  tags = merge(
    local.global_tags,
    local.env_tags,
    local.region_tags,
    local.spoke_tags,
    local.local_tags
  )
}

include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}

terraform {
  source = "github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns?ref=v1.1"
}

inputs = {
  is_hub          = false
  org             = local.env_vars.org
  spoke_def       = local.spoke_vars.spoke
  release_name    = local.local_vars.release_name
  namespace       = local.local_vars.namespace
  sts_assume_role = local.local_vars.sts_assume_role

  region                   = try(local.local_vars.region, "us-east-1")
  domain_name              = try(local.local_vars.domain_name, "example.com")
  domain_name_alias_prefix = try(local.local_vars.domain_name_alias_prefix, "")
  default_domain_ttl       = try(local.local_vars.default_domain_ttl, 300)
  domain_name_weight       = try(local.local_vars.domain_name_weight, -1)
  domain_check_target      = try(local.local_vars.domain_check_target, true)
  domain_alias             = try(local.local_vars.domain_alias, false)
  alias_cname              = try(local.local_vars.alias_cname, "")
  alias_zone_id            = try(local.local_vars.alias_zone_id, "")
  health_check_id          = try(local.local_vars.health_check_id, "")
  private_domain           = try(local.local_vars.private_domain, false)

  extra_tags = local.tags
}
```

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `fqdn` | Fully qualified domain name of the record created, whichever variant was selected. |

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- [Terragrunt](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/) and OpenTofu / Terraform installed.
- An existing Route53 hosted zone matching `domain_name` — this module looks the zone up,
  it does not create it.
- AWS credentials able to assume the role given in `sts_assume_role`.
- A CloudOps Works Terragrunt hierarchy providing `global-`, `env-`, `region-` and
  `spoke-inputs.yaml` plus their matching `*-tags.json` files.

### Steps

```sh
# 1. Create the deployment directory
mkdir -p dev/us-east-1/apps/beanstalk-dns
cd dev/us-east-1/apps/beanstalk-dns

# 2. Scaffold from this module
terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-aws-beanstalk-dns

# 3. Set the minimum required values in inputs.yaml:
#      sts_assume_role, release_name, namespace,
#      domain_name, domain_name_alias_prefix, alias_cname
vi inputs.yaml

# 4. Review the plan, then apply
terragrunt plan
terragrunt apply
```

The `fqdn` output returns the full record name created, ready to be consumed by
downstream deployments.

### Working on the module itself

```sh
make fmt      # format terraform/opentofu code
make lint     # validate and lint
make readme   # regenerate README.md from README.yaml
```


## Examples

All examples below are `inputs.yaml` fragments. Only the keys relevant to each scenario
are shown; the rest keep their defaults.

### Plain CNAME record

Point `app.example.com` at an Elastic Beanstalk environment CNAME with a 5 minute TTL.

```yaml
release_name: "myapp"
namespace: "dev"
domain_name: "example.com"
domain_name_alias_prefix: "app"
alias_cname: "myapp-dev.us-east-1.elasticbeanstalk.com"
default_domain_ttl: 300
domain_check_target: false
```

### Weighted CNAME for blue/green traffic splitting

Deploy this twice — once per environment — with the same `domain_name_alias_prefix` and
different `release_name` / `namespace` pairs, so each deployment owns its own record set
identifier. Weights are relative, so `80` and `20` split traffic 80/20.

```yaml
# Blue deployment
release_name: "myapp"
namespace: "blue"
domain_name: "example.com"
domain_name_alias_prefix: "app"
alias_cname: "myapp-blue.us-east-1.elasticbeanstalk.com"
domain_name_weight: 80
```

```yaml
# Green deployment
release_name: "myapp"
namespace: "green"
domain_name: "example.com"
domain_name_alias_prefix: "app"
alias_cname: "myapp-green.us-east-1.elasticbeanstalk.com"
domain_name_weight: 20
```

### Alias A record with target health evaluation

Alias records need the hosted zone ID of the **target** resource. Leaving
`health_check_id` empty while `domain_check_target` is `true` turns on
`evaluate_target_health`, so Route53 follows the health of the load balancer itself.

```yaml
release_name: "myapp"
namespace: "prod"
domain_name: "example.com"
domain_name_alias_prefix: "www"
domain_alias: true
alias_cname: "dualstack.myapp-prod-1234567890.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com"
alias_zone_id: "Z35SXDOTRQ7X7K"
domain_check_target: true
```

### Weighted alias records with an explicit health check

Combining `domain_alias` with a non-negative `domain_name_weight` yields a weighted
alias record. Supplying `health_check_id` associates an existing Route53 health check
instead of evaluating target health.

```yaml
release_name: "myapp"
namespace: "prod-use1"
domain_name: "example.com"
domain_name_alias_prefix: "www"
domain_alias: true
alias_cname: "dualstack.myapp-use1-1234567890.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com"
alias_zone_id: "Z35SXDOTRQ7X7K"
domain_name_weight: 50
domain_check_target: true
health_check_id: "abcdef12-3456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"
```

### Private hosted zone

Resolve an internal zone of the same name instead of the public one.

```yaml
release_name: "myapp"
namespace: "internal"
domain_name: "example.com"
domain_name_alias_prefix: "api"
alias_cname: "internal-myapp-1234567890.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com"
private_domain: true
```
